column1: Why does naive attention require O(N²) HBM memory?
column2: It writes the full N×N attention score matrix to HBM between the QK and softmax-AV matmuls.

column1: What two scalars does online softmax track per row?
column2: m (running max of logits) and l (running sum of exp(logit - m)).

column1: How does FlashAttention-2 reduce HBM traffic to O(N)?
column2: It tiles Q, K, V within SRAM, runs online softmax tile-by-tile, and writes only the output O and logsumexp back to HBM — never the N×N intermediate.

What is the Triton @triton.jit decorator's primary role?
column2: It JIT-compiles a tile-parallel Python function into warp-level GPU instructions for the target architecture.

column1: What are the two Hopper features FlashAttention-3 exploits that FA2 cannot use?
column2: Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) for async SRAM loads, and warp-group specialization that pipelines async memory transfers with MMA computation.

column1: What speedup does FlashAttention-2 provide over PyTorch naive attention at long sequences?
column2: Roughly 2–4× wall-clock, depending on sequence length and hardware.

column1: What FlashAttention backward-pass trick avoids storing the N×N matrix?
column2: Recomputing attention scores from the saved logsumexp scalar rather than storing the materialized softmax matrix.

column1: Can FlashAttention-3 run on Ampere (A100) GPUs?
column2: No — FA3 requires Hopper-specific hardware (H100 or later).

column1: What does torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention use on Ampere+ with CUDA >= 11.6?
column2: It automatically dispatches to FlashAttention-2 when available.
